label: copy-phase input y or 2 (sparse subset)
explanation: Sparse feature (0.16% of steps). About 86% of activation mass is in the copy phase, and it is dominated by the input token: y (16x lift, 51% of mass) and 2 (7x lift, 22%), with l a weaker third. Copy-phase steps whose input is y or 2 cover about 71% of activation mass, but only about 4% of those steps fire, so precision is very low. Conditioning on prev_tok (a/p/i), out_tok, position (to_go, recall_idx) or digit count raised precision only to about 10-20% while giving up most of the recall, so the gating context was not found. Rate rises toward late copy steps (t = 16-17, recall_idx 7-8), and the largest activations are on y. A small original-phase component exists, mostly at t = 3 (about 9% of mass). It almost never fires at t < 2 or on the delimiter step.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=15: y, 2, l, h; t=16: y, 2, l, k; t=11: y, 2, l, h) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: 0, h, y, 2; delimiter step: 0, y, 2, q; input phase: ); timing cues that raise it most: t=3, t=4, L=8 & t=9.
